CCC Launches CCC® Intelligent Reinspection to Help Auto Insurers Review Repair Estimates Faster, Expediting Repairer Workflows and Claims Resolutions | CCC Intelligent Solutions

## CCC Launches CCC® Intelligent Reinspection to Help Auto Insurers Review Repair Estimates Faster, Expediting Repairer Workflows and Claims Resolutions

July 30, 2024 at 8:00 AM EDT

AI-Powered Solution Streamlines Estimate Reviews and Helps Get Drivers Back on the Road Sooner Following an Accident

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 30, 2024-- CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc.(CCC), a leading cloud platform powering the P&C insurance economy, announces today the launch of CCC® Intelligent Reinspection, a new solution designed to help auto insurers streamline the review of incoming repair facility estimates, expediting repairer workflows and claims resolutions. Leveraging advanced AI technology, CCC Intelligent Reinspection identifies areas for review, and provides reason codes based on insurer rules, helping reinspectors review increasingly complex estimates quickly, reducing repair and claim cycle times so drivers can get back on the road sooner following a car accident.

“The increasing complexity of vehicles today requires advanced solutions to streamline the claims and repair process,” said John Goodson, chief product and technology officer for CCC. “With CCC Intelligent Reinspection, AI helps insurers review repair estimates more quickly and transparently, allowing them to resolve questions with their repair partners. Our solution integrates seamlessly into existing insurer and repairer workflows, so estimates turn into completed repairs and claims can be resolved faster.”

Using AI-powered analysis and audit capabilities, CCC Intelligent Reinspection assesses incoming shop estimates based on insurer-provided rules. It automatically routes estimates for approval or review, significantly reducing manual workloads for appraisers and desk reviewers. This fosters better collaboration between insurers and repairers, helping to provide timely and accurate feedback without disrupting workflows, helping both save valuable time. CCC’s AI, developed over ten years and used broadly across collision repairers and insurers, employs computer vision and other advanced AI technologies to analyze photos of vehicle damage along with the repair estimate, improving accuracy and supporting repairers’ commitment to quality repairs.

“CCC Intelligent Reinspection represents a significant advancement in how repair estimates are managed between insurers and repairers,” Goodson added. “Our AI-powered solution makes it easy for estimates to be quickly reviewed so repairers can get to work faster. Intelligent Reinspection is the latest in a line of intelligent, AI-driven solutions from CCC designed to save time and reduce inefficiencies in the increasingly complex claims and repair process, supporting our vision of shaping a world where life just works for our customers and theirs.”

Key benefits of CCC Intelligent Reinspection include:

Seamless Integration: Connects effortlessly to existing reinspection processes, enabling continuity and efficiency.

Improved Review Efficiency: Provides reason codes based on individual insurer rules, supporting more efficient and transparent reviews and insurer, shop communications.

Reduced Cycle Times: Helps reduce the time required for claim resolutions, enabling faster service for consumers.

About CCC

CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC), a subsidiary of CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: CCCS), is a leading cloud platform for the multi-trillion-dollar P&C insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. The CCC Intelligent Experience (IX) Cloud™ platform, powered by proven AI and an innovative event-based architecture, connects more than 35,000 businesses to power customized applications and platforms for optimal outcomes and personalized experiences that just work. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at www.cccis.com.

## CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

October 29, 2026 at 7:05 AM EDT 
CHICAGO, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. (“CCC” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: CCC), a leading 
SaaS and AI platform provider for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, today announced its financial results for the three months ended 
September 30, 2026. 
“CCC delivered strong third quarter results, with revenue growth of 10% and adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 44%. Our performance reflects 
the durability of our business, the trust customers place in us, and the increasing role our platform plays in helping participants across the insurance 
economy operate more efficiently and achieve better outcomes,” said Githesh Ramamurthy, Chairman & CEO of CCC. 
“The pending transaction with GTCR and Elliott marks an exciting next chapter for CCC and our customers,” continued Ramamurthy. “Together, we 
expect to accelerate the AI and agentic capabilities our customers want from us, expand the network at the center of our platform, and make long-term 
investments in innovation that help customers navigate growing complexity across the claims lifecycle. We believe this positions CCC to deliver even 
greater value to the insurance economy in the years ahead.” 
Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights 
Revenue 
• Total revenue was $294.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 10.1% from $267.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. 

Profitability

• GAAP gross profit was $218.0 million, representing a gross margin of 74%, for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $193.0 million, representing a gross margin of 72%, for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted gross profit was $224.6 million, representing an adjusted gross profit margin of 76%, for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $199.5 million, representing an adjusted gross profit margin of 78%, for the third quarter of 2025. 
• GAAP operating income was $57.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with GAAP operating income of $30.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted operating income was $115.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with adjusted operating income of $93.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. 

• GAAP net income was $30.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with GAAP net loss of $2.0 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted net income was $75.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $59.4 million for the third quarter of 2025.

• Adjusted EBITDA was $130.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, up 18.5% compared with adjusted EBITDA of $110.1 million for the third quarter of 2025.

Liquidity

• CCC had $202.9 million in cash and cash equivalents and $1.28 billion of total debt as of September 30, 2026. The Company generated $100.4 million in cash from operating activities and had free cash flow of $82.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $94.8 million in cash generated from operating activities and free cash flow of $78.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. 

3rd Quarter and Recent Business Highlights

GTCR and Elliott to acquire CCC. On October 15, 2026, CCC announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in an all-cash transaction in which shareholders will receive $7.75 per share, representing an enterprise value of approximately $6.1 billion. Subject to regulatory and stockholder approvals and other customary closing conditions, the proposed transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Following the close, CCC will become a privately held company. Insurers expand AI adoption across core claims workflows. CCC’s AI-related revenue reached approximately $130 million in annualized run-rate in the third quarter of 2026, representing growth of 40% year over year and increasing from an annualized run rate of approximately $120 million in the second quarter of 2026. This growth reflects a continuing shift in customer behavior from AI experimentation to AI deployment at scale. Leading insurer is largest to adopt Medhub for Auto Casualty. During the third quarter of 2026, a top-five insurer (based on 2025 direct premium written) became the largest insurer to adopt CCC’s Medhub for Auto Casualty, which uses

AI to extract critical insights from complex medical records and help claims professionals make faster, more informed decisions grounded in auditable claim data. The deployment marks the largest application of EvolutionIQ’s technology within the P&C auto market and demonstrates customers’ willingness to adopt adjacent workflows from CCC, underscoring the substantial growth opportunity beyond the traditional APD business.

# CCC Intelligent Solutions Signs Definitive Agreement to Be Acquired by GTCR and Elliott

Stockholders to Receive $7.75 Per Share in Cash

CHICAGO - October 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: CCC) (“CCC” or the “Company”), a leading SaaS and AI platform provider for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR, and including Elliott Investment Management L.P. (together with its affiliates, “Elliott”), in an all-cash transaction with an enterprise value of approximately $6.1 billion.

Under the terms of the agreement, CCC stockholders will receive $7.75 in cash for each share of CCC common stock, representing a premium of approximately 44% to CCC’s unaffected closing stock price on July 9, 2026, the last trading day prior to media speculation regarding a potential sale of the Company, and a premium of approximately 59% to the 30-day average price as of July 9, 2026.

Based in Chicago, CCC connects more than 35,000 businesses across the insurance economy. Drawing on 40 years of industry data and over a decade of AI embedded into mission-critical workflows, CCC helps customers improve decision-making, efficiency and outcomes across the claims and repair lifecycle.

“Throughout CCC’s history, we have helped customers navigate growing complexity and achieve better outcomes through technology and innovation,” said Githesh Ramamurthy, Chairman & CEO of CCC. “With GTCR and Elliott’s experience and resources, we will continue to build on our momentum and extend our leadership. Together, we will accelerate the AI and agentic capabilities our customers want from us, expand the network at the center of our platform, and continue to develop and build our world class team. I am deeply grateful to our employees for their dedication and commitment to our customers, and I am excited for all that we will accomplish together in this next chapter.”

Ramamurthy added, “Today’s announcement follows a thorough review of strategic options with assistance from our financial and legal advisors. Our Board of Directors is confident this transaction recognizes the strength of the business our team has built while delivering immediate and premium cash value to our stockholders.”

“We have followed CCC for years and believe the Company is uniquely positioned to support their customers as they increasingly adopt AI solutions to improve decision making and efficiency across the claims and repair lifecycle,” said Mark Anderson, Managing Director, Head of Technology, Media & Telecommunications at GTCR. “We look forward to partnering with Githesh and the talented CCC team to support continued investment in product innovation and AI capabilities, expand the Company’s offerings and build long-term value. Our focus will be on helping CCC deliver better outcomes for its customers while supporting CCC’s next phase of growth.”

“We have strong belief in CCC’s position as the trusted third party at the center of the automotive insurance and repair industry,” said David Kerko, Head of Global Private Equity at Elliott. “CCC’s role within the large ecosystem of insurers, repair facilities, automakers and parts suppliers creates strong data advantages and network benefits for their more than 35,000 customers. We believe these advantages make CCC a highly durable franchise in vertical software – which AI will only make more valuable as CCC delivers the next generation of capabilities to its customers.”

Transaction Approvals and Timing

The transaction was approved by CCC’s Board of Directors and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including the receipt of required regulatory approvals and the approval of CCC stockholders. Until the transaction closes, CCC remains publicly traded and will continue operating as an independent company. The transaction is not subject to a financing condition. Upon completion of the transaction, CCC will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on the Nasdaq.

Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Results

CCC will release its third quarter 2026 financial results on October 29, 2026. In light of the pending transaction, the Company will not host a conference call or webcast to discuss the results.

Advisors

Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC is serving as financial advisor, Kirkland & Ellis LLP is serving as legal counsel, and Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor to CCC.

J.P. Morgan is serving as lead financial advisor to GTCR and lead arranger of committed financing for the transaction. Citi is also serving as financial advisor and participating in the committed financing. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP is serving as legal counsel to GTCR, and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP and Debevoise & Plimpton LLP are serving as legal counsel to Elliott.

# Debt Drive: CCC buyout may push interest payments up

CRM Editor November 13, 2026

The buyers of Chicago-based collision repair software supplier CCC Intelligent Solutions are arranging US$2.85 billion in borrowing to help finance a takeover that could push the business’s annual interest bill to approximately US$250 million.

That would mean an increase of more than US$150 million in annual cash interest costs in 2027, according to a Nov. 10 assessment by S&P Global Ratings.

The financing would support the acquisition announced Oct. 15 by a group led by Chicago-based private equity firm GTCR and including Florida-based Elliott Investment Management. Existing CCC debt would also be refinanced.

JPMorgan launched the financing Nov. 9, according to a Nov. 11 report by leveraged-finance news service LCD.

CCC is the supplier behind CCC ONE, software used to write estimates, source parts, receive insurance assignments and manage repairs. The broader CCC network connects more than 35,000 businesses, including insurers, repairers, automakers and parts suppliers.

Under the takeover agreement, shareholders would receive US$7.75 in cash per share. CCC would become privately owned and stop trading on Nasdaq.

The transaction carries an enterprise value of approximately US$6.1 billion, a figure that includes debt and other adjustments. The US$2.85-billion borrowing package forms part of the financing, alongside money from investors.

The arrangement is a leveraged buyout: buyers borrow to help purchase a business, then rely on its future cash flow to support the debt.

The financial burden would extend beyond interest.

S&P analysts forecast that cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investment would fall to between US$35 million and US$45 million in 2027, from approximately US$300 million in 2026. Cash payments for employees’ previously awarded share-based compensation would also contribute to the decline.

The analysts assigned a B-minus credit rating with a stable outlook to Mozart Merger Sub, the acquisition entity initially taking on the borrowing, and its proposed secured term loan.

A B-category rating signals greater vulnerability to difficult business or economic conditions, although the borrower currently has the capacity to meet its obligations.

S&P analysts expect sufficient liquidity to cover the payments and an improvement in financial measures in 2028 as revenue grows and some compensation costs decline.

The borrowing would be supported by a business built largely on recurring subscription fees.

CCC’s quarterly filings show that software subscriptions accounted for approximately 96% of revenue in the three months ended Sept. 30. Revenue reached US$294.1 million, up 10.1% from a year earlier, largely through existing customers upgrading or buying additional products.

Net income was US$30.2 million, compared with a US$2-million loss a year earlier. Debt stood at approximately US$1.28 billion at quarter-end, before the proposed takeover financing.

Githesh Ramamurthy, CCC chairman and chief executive officer, and Tim Welsh, president, have agreed to exchange some of their CCC shares for ownership interests in the buyer’s holding structure.

“With GTCR and Elliott’s experience and resources, we will continue to build on our momentum and extend our leadership,” Ramamurthy said in the acquisition announcement.

Completion is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder approval, regulatory requirements and other closing conditions.
